designs.title: Pisa
designs.why: Clean, well-crafted one-ink line work: the tower's arcades, belfry and diamond inlays hold up at full size, the serif PISA header is confident, and the details are smart (3.97 deg as the 'denomination', a 9 VIII 1173 cancel for the founding date, wavy cancel lines running over the perforation). It reverses well on black. But the real hook, the lean, barely registers from 3 m: a 4 deg tower inside an upright frame just reads as a slightly off drawing, so the 3.97 deg joke needs explaining. The stamp-of-a-landmark format is also a familiar souvenir-shop template, and the upper-right of the stamp is dead space beside the tower. At $50 it reads as a nice museum-shop tee, not yet a label piece.
designs.fix: Make the lean the graphic: add a thin dashed vertical plumb line from the tower's crown down to the base with a small angle arc labelled 3.97 deg between it and the tower's axis. That fills the empty right side, makes the denomination joke land at a glance, and turns a postcard into an idea.
